subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should macOS Gateway LaunchAgents include Nix/user package-manager bin dirs by default, expose a narrow opt-in/Nix-mode service PATH path, or keep the canonical PATH and update docs?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally harden the macOS service PATH, but public Nix docs promise macOS launchd Nix-profile discovery; changing the default affects daemon command-resolution trust.

options.title: Add narrow opt-in or Nix-mode support
options.body: Keep the canonical macOS default, but add maintainer-approved Nix/profile support behind an explicit trusted path and align doctor, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Broaden the macOS default
options.body: Include user and Nix bin dirs automatically on macOS, accepting the larger command-resolution trust surface as intentional product behavior.

options.title: Keep canonical PATH and fix docs
options.body: Leave the hardened macOS service PATH unchanged and update Nix/install docs to direct operators to supported explicit PATH controls instead.

recommendation.title: Add narrow opt-in or Nix-mode support
recommendation.body: Keep the canonical macOS default, but add maintainer-approved Nix/profile support behind an explicit trusted path and align doctor, docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent maintainer-visible service PATH precedence decision on the adjacent active PATH PR makes this the best available routing signal.
